name: MCL Compression to Liquidity Release
hypothesis: Oil may offer a distinct event-driven edge when a completed low-efficiency one-hour auction compresses relative to its completed six-hour context and then releases through a range/volume shock whose dominant CL and executable MCL books agree; CL/MCL basis response categorically distinguishes acceptance from failed-auction fade.

state_machine.clock: completed five-minute dated CL and matched-suffix MCL bars
state_machine.context: prior 72 completed bars; recent window is the last 12
state_machine.compression: recent median CL true range <= 72-bar median and recent close-path efficiency <=0.35
state_machine.arming: arm only on a new compression episode; after one release, require compression to end before rearming
state_machine.release_range: current completed CL true range >=2x the prior 12-bar median
state_machine.release_volume: current completed CL volume >=2x the prior 12-bar median
state_machine.parity: current CL and MCL open-to-close moves have the same nonzero sign and both bars have positive volume
state_machine.entry_readiness: next one-minute same-suffix MCL open exists outside the 16:25–18:00 ET admission blackout
state_machine.direction: raw release sign when directional MCL-minus-CL basis velocity is nonnegative; fade the raw release when executable MCL lags dominant CL
state_machine.branch: follow is acceptance; fade is failure

selection_law: Choose the first profile clearing every count-only gate in both periods. Range plus volume precedes the range-only sensitivity control. No outcome may select a profile.
if_eligible: Freeze one exact lifecycle family before opening PnL; the nonselected cadence profile remains a count control and cannot rescue outcomes.
if_ineligible: Reject this exact compression-release clock before outcomes; do not sweep efficiency, range, volume, context, refractory, or cadence floors.
